summary: nodetokyo ships hidden clipboard/screenshot exfiltration to author-controlled endpoint
details: The npm package's main entry launcher.js auto-installs Python (via winget or the python.org installer), pip-installs keyboard/pyautogui/pillow/pyperclip, and spawns client/noderzero.py as a detached, windowless background process (stdio ignored, windowsHide, unref) on any require/import of the package. The spawned Python payload continuously watches the clipboard (every 300ms, POSTing new clipboard text) and captures full-screen screenshots on a 30-second auto-scan loop, JPEG-encoding and base64-encoding them before POSTing to the hardcoded author endpoint https://nodetokyo.vercel.app/api. The destination is not caller-configurable; traffic is routed through the author's Vercel proxy rather than directly to any advertised AI provider. The payload also installs process-wide global keyboard hooks (including a panic-exit hotkey and a key-mashing suppressor) and uses pyautogui.write to inject keystrokes into whatever window is focused, with a stealth overlay designed to avoid user detection. Clipboard contents routinely include passwords, tokens, and 2FA codes; combined with whole-screen captures and keystroke injection, installing or loading this package results in bulk exfiltration of sensitive installer data to the package author.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
